questions.q: What is a cloud Region, such as AWS's us-east-1 or Azure's eastus?
options: A single physical server
A geographic area where a cloud provider operates a cluster of datacenters
A type of virtual machine size
A billing category with no physical meaning
questions.explain: A region is a large geographic area — like Northern Virginia for AWS's us-east-1 — where the provider runs a cluster of datacenters.

options: A marketing term with no technical meaning
One isolated datacenter, or small cluster of them, within a region, with independent power, cooling, and networking
The same thing as a region, just a different name
A single rack inside one datacenter
questions.explain: An AZ is a physically distinct facility within a region, built with independent power, cooling, and network connectivity so a failure in one doesn't reach the others.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, why did the e-commerce site stay online when the datacenter behind us-east-1a lost power?
options: Because AWS datacenters never lose power
Because its second web server was in a different Availability Zone, us-east-1b, and the load balancer routed traffic there
Because the application was written in a faster programming language
Because us-east-1a and us-east-1b are actually the same physical building
questions.explain: Placing the second server in a separate AZ meant the load balancer could fail traffic over to the healthy server when the first AZ's datacenter lost power.

questions.q: What would have happened if both of the e-commerce site's web servers had been placed in us-east-1a alone?
options: Nothing — a single AZ provides the same protection as multiple AZs
The entire site would have gone down when that one datacenter lost power
The load balancer would have created a third server automatically
The site would have run faster
questions.explain: With both servers in the same AZ, a failure in that one facility takes down every instance of the application at once.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between a multi-AZ deployment and a multi-region deployment?
options: They are the same thing with different names
Multi-AZ is the low-cost baseline protecting against one facility failing; multi-region is a bigger step protecting against a regional disaster and improving global latency
Multi-region is always cheaper than multi-AZ
Multi-AZ only works for Azure, and multi-region only works for AWS
questions.explain: Multi-AZ is the standard baseline resilience most production workloads should have. Multi-region adds protection against a whole-region disaster and can help with global latency, at added cost and complexity.
